keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «알림이 깊이 집중하는 능력을 조용히 떨어뜨린다(주장)» 와 «필요 없는 알림을 끄거나 휴대폰을 다른 방에 두면 집중을 지킬 수 있다(해결책)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the claim (notifications quietly reduce our ability to focus deeply) and the solution (turning off non-essential alerts or keeping the phone in another room). The green sentences are the answers.

qs.q: Why can even an alert we choose to ignore pull part of our mind away?
qs.qko: 왜 무시하기로 한 알림조차 우리 마음의 일부를 끌어갈 수 있나요?
opts: Because the phone gets louder each time
Because we start wondering what the alert says
Because app designers turn off the screen
evs: Each alert seems harmless, since it takes only a second to glance at the screen.
Even an alert we choose to ignore can pull part of our mind away, because we start wondering what it says.
Most of these checks are triggered by notifications: a buzz, a sound, or a red badge on an app icon.
why: 본문에 «we start wondering what it says» 라고 나와요. 무엇이라고 쓰여 있는지 궁금해지기 때문에 마음이 끌려가요.
The text says we start wondering what the alert says, so part of our mind is pulled away.

qs.q: In the text, what does 'attention residue' mean?
qs.qko: 글에서 'attention residue(주의 잔여물)' 는 무슨 뜻인가요?
opts: Part of our mind still stays on the earlier distraction
A red badge that stays on an app icon
The total number of alerts in one day
evs: When we switch from a task to a message, our brain needs time to return fully to what we were doing.
Psychologists call this lingering distraction 'attention residue.'
Most of these checks are triggered by notifications: a buzz, a sound, or a red badge on an app icon.
Our attention is limited, so it is worth deciding for ourselves where it goes.
why: 메시지로 옮겨 갔다가 원래 일로 완전히 돌아오는 데 시간이 걸린다고 하고, 그 «남아 있는 산만함» 을 attention residue 라고 불러요.
The brain needs time to return fully to the task, and this lingering distraction is called attention residue.

qs.q: Why does the writer say we should decide for ourselves where our attention goes?
qs.qko: 글쓴이는 왜 우리의 주의를 어디에 쓸지 스스로 정해야 한다고 말하나요?
opts: Because attention is limited and apps are designed to pull it back
Because phones break easily if they are used too often
Because research shows notifications improve memory
evs: App designers know this, and many notifications are built to feel urgent so that users return to the app.
Our attention is limited, so it is worth deciding for ourselves where it goes.
Many people check their phones dozens of times a day, often without thinking about it.
why: 앱 알림은 사용자가 앱으로 돌아오도록 급하게 느껴지게 만들어지고, 우리의 주의는 한정되어 있어요. 두 단서를 합치면 스스로 정해야 하는 이유가 나와요.
Apps build alerts to feel urgent so users return, and our attention is limited. Together these explain why we should choose for ourselves.

ends: How do app designers make alerts feel urgent?

write.moreKo: 한 걸음 더: «we can» 뒤에 «동사 + 무엇을» 쓰고, 시간이나 횟수를 더해 보세요. (예: focus on reading for an hour)
write.moreEn: One more step: after «we can», write a verb + what, and add a time or number. (e.g. focus on reading for an hour)
